item.title: Renormalisation Group: Glossary
item.description: A plain-language glossary for the renormalisation group course: every technical word explained in one or two simple sentences, with an everyday picture and a pointer to where the course explains it properly.

item.title: Renormalisation Group V: Wilson's Momentum Shells
item.description: Part 5 of the renormalisation group course. From spins to a smooth field, Wilson's three-step RG in momentum space explained as filtering music and zooming out, the free-field (Gaussian) fixed point, power counting and why four dimensions is special.

item.title: Renormalisation Group VII: Running Couplings
item.description: Part 7 of the renormalisation group course. The particle physics road, in simple words: counterterms, minimal subtraction, beta functions and the Callan-Symanzik equation. phi^4 finds the Wilson-Fisher point again, QED screens (checked with FORM and Wolfram) and QCD antiscreens and is asymptotically free. With an interactive running-coupling calculator.

item.title: Renormalisation Group IV: Fixed Points and Universality
item.description: Part 4 of the renormalisation group course. What a critical point looks like, why it is a fixed point of the RG, relevant and irrelevant directions as a ball on a mountain ridge, critical exponents from one number, universality as a river basin and the exact 2D critical temperature from a mirror symmetry. With a live 2D Ising simulation you can coarse-grain.

item.title: Renormalisation Group III: Block Spins
item.description: Part 3 of the renormalisation group course. Kadanoff's block-spin idea done exactly on a line of spins, explained as a game of telephone: the recursion tanh K' = tanh^2 K, fixed points and a correlation length that never changes when you measure it properly. With an interactive widget.

item.title: Renormalisation Group II: Loops, Infinities and Cutoffs
item.description: Part 2 of the renormalisation group course. The toolkit from zero, with a picture for each idea: where loop integrals come from, the Wick rotation done as a real contour integral, why loops blow up, what a cutoff is, three ways to regularise the same integral and what renormalisation actually does. With an interactive cutoff widget.

item.title: Renormalisation Group I: Why Scale Matters
item.description: Part 1 of the renormalisation group course. A quantum correction to a particle's mass, worked out diagram by diagram, comes out infinite. What that is really telling us about coupling constants and the scale we look at.

item.title: The Renormalisation Group: a beginner's course
item.description: An eight-part beginner's course on the renormalisation group, in simple words with an everyday picture for every idea: loops and cutoffs from scratch, block spins and the Ising chain, fixed points and universality, Wilson's momentum shells, the Wilson-Fisher fixed point, running couplings in QED and QCD and effective field theory. Every formula checked in Wolfram and FORM, with live simulations in the browser.

item.title: Renormalisation Group VIII: Effective Field Theory
item.description: Part 8 of the renormalisation group course. Why physics works at all without a final theory: effective field theories as a multipole expansion, Fermi's theory as the low-energy shadow of the W boson, what renormalisable really means, why high-energy physics is hard, triviality, asymptotic freedom and safety, naturalness and where to go next.

item.title: Renormalisation Group VI: The Wilson-Fisher Fixed Point
item.description: Part 6 of the renormalisation group course. The one-loop momentum-shell RG of phi^4 theory, step by step, the flow equations read as a population with limited food, the Wilson-Fisher fixed point in d = 4 - epsilon and critical exponents compared with experiment. With an interactive flow diagram.

item.title: Tree Codes 4: Results
item.description: Part 4 of recreating Hernquist (1987): the evolving cluster, timing against N and theta, force errors, softening, conservation laws and relaxation, all measured with my own Julia code.

item.title: Tree Codes 3: The Tree and the Multipole Expansion
item.description: Part 3 of recreating Hernquist (1987): building an octree, the opening criterion and the multipole expansion derived term by term from the Legendre generating function.

item.title: Tree Codes 6: Doing Better Than 1987
item.description: Part 6 of recreating Hernquist (1987): going past the paper with octupole multipoles, a fourth-order symplectic integrator and a million particles.

item.title: Tree Codes: Recreating Hernquist (1987)
item.description: Recreating Hernquist's 1987 paper on the performance of Barnes-Hut tree codes, from scratch in Julia: the Plummer model, the leapfrog integrator, the multipole expansion and every timing and error test in the paper.

item.title: Tree Codes 2: Moving the Particles
item.description: Part 2 of recreating Hernquist (1987): deriving the leapfrog integrator from Taylor expansions, and why this second-order scheme beats Runge-Kutta 4 for gravitational N-body work.

item.title: Tree Codes 1: The Problem and the Model
item.description: Part 1 of recreating Hernquist (1987): Poisson's equation, the Plummer sphere, sampling initial conditions from a distribution function and the virial theorem.

item.title: Tree Codes 5: The Code
item.description: Part 5 of recreating Hernquist (1987): the complete Julia source for the Barnes-Hut tree code, the test suite and how to run everything yourself.

item.title: The Expanding Universe I — Geometry
item.description: Part 1 of The Expanding Universe. Deriving the Robertson–Walker metric from scratch — the embedding of the symmetric three-spaces, the reduction to a(t) and k, the S_k(χ) curvature function and conformal time — with the expansion history, horizon and curvature radius computed in Cosmic.jl.

item.title: The Expanding Universe II — Kinematics
item.description: Part 2 of The Expanding Universe. Deriving the geodesic equation, the E ∝ 1/a redshift, the Hubble–Lemaître law, and the luminosity and angular-diameter distances from first principles — with distances for flat, open and closed universes all computed in Cosmic.jl.

item.title: The Expanding Universe with Cosmic.jl
item.description: A five-part tour through cosmology (Baumann, Chapters 2, 5 and 6): the homogeneous universe's geometry, kinematics, dynamics and thermal history, then how tiny perturbations grow into galaxies — with every result checked numerically against my Julia package Cosmic.jl.

item.title: The Expanding Universe V — Perturbations
item.description: Part 5 of The Expanding Universe. Deriving the growth of structure — the Newtonian fluid equations, the relativistic generalisation in the conformal Newtonian gauge, gauge freedom, and the Mészáros effect — with the growth factor, the perturbation hierarchy and the matter power spectrum all computed in Cosmic.jl.

item.title: The Expanding Universe IV — Our Universe
item.description: Part 4 of The Expanding Universe. The measured cosmic budget, the age, matter–radiation equality, and the thermal history — deriving the photon density and the Saha recombination equation, with the ionization history, last scattering and the BAO sound horizon computed in Cosmic.jl against Baumann's Table 2.1.

item.title: The Expanding Universe III — Dynamics
item.description: Part 3 of The Expanding Universe. Deriving the continuity equation, the Friedmann equations and the exact radiation/matter/Λ solutions — with the density eras, the expansion history, and the fate of flat, open and closed universes all computed in Cosmic.jl.
